text: A group's leader uploads a segment or a snapshot with put-if-absent, under a name made of the group's incarnation and offset.
evidence: DESIGN-V5 3.4 and 4.1 (not modelled)

text: A segment or snapshot is named in its group's log only after its put is confirmed.
evidence: DESIGN-V5 3.4 and 4.1 (not modelled)

text: A snapshot layer holds the rows changed since the last layer, plus a removal marker for each row removed since.
evidence: DESIGN-V5 3.4 and 4.1 (not modelled)

text: A cold start applies the base, then each layer in order, so a removed row stays removed.
evidence: DESIGN-V5 3.4 and 4.1 (not modelled)

text: A background merge folds layers in order, and drops a removal marker only once no older layer is below it.
evidence: DESIGN-V5 3.4 and 4.1 (not modelled)

text: A single snapshot layer covers nothing by itself: only a merged base, or the copy's own full snapshot, lets the log be dropped.
evidence: DESIGN-V5 4.1 (When a replica may drop its log)

text: A retry from a session older than a restore is refused.
evidence: E-33 (8 of 8 mutants caught, the store always up)

text: A slot move records its new epoch in the store's restore mark before it uses the epoch.
evidence: E-33 (8 of 8 mutants caught, the store always up)

text: A restore takes a slot epoch above the restore mark.
evidence: E-33 (8 of 8 mutants caught, the store always up)

text: A restore starts a new session generation.
evidence: E-33 (8 of 8 mutants caught, the store always up)

text: A cursor that the restored history does not hold is refused.
evidence: E-33 (8 of 8 mutants caught, the store always up)

text: W1, intent: the saga library starts a unit's steps only once its intent row has committed, never on an early answer.
evidence: E-48 (W1 model-checked on another system's steps; its mapping onto sagas is reasoned, V5-5)

text: W1, step: the saga library sends each next step, the undo decision, each undo and the end only once the write before it has committed.
evidence: E-48 (W1 model-checked on another system's steps; its mapping onto sagas is reasoned, V5-5)

text: W1, check: a holder that carries on or resolves another unit acts only on committed reads of that unit's intent and lock rows.
evidence: E-48 (W1 model-checked on another system's steps; its mapping onto sagas is reasoned, V5-5)

text: W1, claim: a write under a lock is sent only once the lock's claim has committed.
evidence: E-48 (W1 model-checked on another system's steps; its mapping onto sagas is reasoned, V5-5)

text: Y: a writer's read waits until its last early-answered write is committed and visible, or known lost.
evidence: E-48 (Y, needed alone)

text: A follower reports a batch as in memory only after it has handed the batch to the operating system.
evidence: MEMORY 9.4 (not modelled)

text: The leader counts its own copy toward replicated only after its own write call for that batch.
evidence: MEMORY 9.4 (not modelled)

text: The leader's replicated mark is the highest entry a majority holds in memory, and a replicated answer comes only from that mark.
evidence: MEMORY 9.4 (not modelled)

text: Commit never reads the replicated mark: it moves only on disk reports.
evidence: MEMORY 9.4 (not modelled)

text: A received answer comes only after the leader has appended the write, never on arrival.
evidence: MEMORY 9.4 (not modelled)

text: The client keeps an early-answered write pending until it commits, and sends it again after a failover.
evidence: MEMORY 9.4 (not modelled)

text: Only a write that cannot be refused takes an early stage: a whole-row set or remove with no condition, no once name and no mark, on a resource with no write rules.
evidence: MEMORY 9.4 (not modelled)

text: Each subject is delivered through one ordering point: the group that holds its slot.
evidence: REQUIREMENTS P-06; AMENDMENTS K-10 (the failover rule is unwritten and unmodelled)

text: A message goes to every subscriber registered there when it arrives, in order, at most once.
evidence: REQUIREMENTS P-06; AMENDMENTS K-10 (the failover rule is unwritten and unmodelled)

text: A message on this rung is never written to the log, and its publish answers no more than sent.
evidence: REQUIREMENTS P-06; AMENDMENTS K-10 (the failover rule is unwritten and unmodelled)

text: When the subject's slot moves or its server goes, each subscription ends with a notice, so the client subscribes again elsewhere.
evidence: REQUIREMENTS P-06; AMENDMENTS K-10 (the failover rule is unwritten and unmodelled)

text: A fork writes one record per group, naming the parent's snapshot and segments and the position it starts from, and copies nothing.
evidence: DESIGN-V5 6.2 and 4.1; REQUIREMENTS TEST-06, OPS-07; E-06 (the cost measured; not modelled)

text: A fork starts only at a position the parent has committed.
evidence: DESIGN-V5 6.2 and 4.1; REQUIREMENTS TEST-06, OPS-07; E-06 (the cost measured; not modelled)

text: A fork refuses a position below what the parent has already dropped.
evidence: DESIGN-V5 6.2 and 4.1; REQUIREMENTS TEST-06, OPS-07; E-06 (the cost measured; not modelled)

text: A fork's record commits before the fork reads any of the parent's files.
evidence: DESIGN-V5 6.2 and 4.1; REQUIREMENTS TEST-06, OPS-07; E-06 (the cost measured; not modelled)

text: The parent drops a snapshot or segment only after checking that no committed fork record names it.
evidence: DESIGN-V5 6.2 and 4.1; REQUIREMENTS TEST-06, OPS-07; E-06 (the cost measured; not modelled)

text: In a fork, each slot comes from the one group that held it open at the fork's cut, so a slot that was moving then is neither lost nor doubled.
evidence: DESIGN-V5 6.2 and 4.1; REQUIREMENTS TEST-06, OPS-07; E-06 (the cost measured; not modelled)

text: A fork writes only new files under its own name and incarnation, and never overwrites or deletes the parent's.
evidence: DESIGN-V5 6.2 and 4.1; REQUIREMENTS TEST-06, OPS-07; E-06 (the cost measured; not modelled)

text: Each leader keeps a latency score for itself and for each follower over a window.
evidence: AMENDMENTS A-03; E-38 finding F-18; REQUIREMENTS F-18 (not built or modelled)

text: A leader whose score stays k times its followers' hands leadership to its most caught-up fast follower.
evidence: AMENDMENTS A-03; E-38 finding F-18; REQUIREMENTS F-18 (not built or modelled)

text: A member that handed off for slowness takes no leadership back, and is no preferred leader, until its score has been normal for a hold time.
evidence: AMENDMENTS A-03; E-38 finding F-18; REQUIREMENTS F-18 (not built or modelled)
